sources.title: MsiBeginTransactionW
sources.paraphrasedFinding: Starts a multiple-package transaction. One process owns it. The event signals ownership transfer by Join; leaving no owner causes rollback. Only one open transaction; Windows Installer4.5+, including Win7 Installer5. This event is not a commit/rollback completion signal.

sources.title: MsiJoinTransaction
sources.paraphrasedFinding: Ownership transfer requires same user and related process tree. It is rejected while an active installation is in progress. A live transaction ID is not a generic capability a running deferred CA can adopt at any phase.

sources.title: MsiEndTransaction
sources.paraphrasedFinding: Only current owner ends the transaction. COMMIT runs commit actions and discards rollback script; ROLLBACK undoes transaction installations. Already-running/failure/rollback-disabled errors exist; an end request alone is not successful settlement.

sources.title: MsiEmbeddedChainer Table
sources.paraphrasedFinding: Embedded EXE functions are referenced by a table in the MSI. The engine passes transaction ID; function must Join and End, otherwise early return causes rollback. Only one matching row may run; type2/18/50 only. Prevent advertisement. Documentation does not explicitly establish a no-additional-package guardian or all direct maintenance-mode invocation points.

sources.title: Multiple-Package Installations
sources.paraphrasedFinding: Installer4.5+ supports joint transactions including product install/configure/reinstall operations. ForceReboot/ScheduleReboot introduce exceptions, so exclude both. These APIs do not by themselves serialize the application data/runtime.

sources.title: InstallFinalize Action
sources.paraphrasedFinding: Runs the outstanding installation script and ends its Initialize transaction. It is an action, not a separately exposed native event proving every custom helper has returned. A standalone package transaction and an explicit outer multiple-package transaction must not be conflated.

sources.title: Commit Custom Actions
sources.paraphrasedFinding: Commit CAs run after successful script processing, but failure can still initiate rollback; they are not all-work-finished notification. Commit/rollback CAs are skipped when rollback disabled; forbid that condition.

sources.title: Rollback Custom Actions
sources.paraphrasedFinding: Rollback CA precedes the deferred action it reverses and must tolerate partial interruption. It runs synchronously during rollback; receiving or returning it is not a documented global rollback-completed signal. It must never alone clear maintenance blockage.

sources.title: RemoveExistingProducts Action
sources.paraphrasedFinding: Old products are removed through concurrent installations. Early-after-Initialize placement permits no intervening script-generating actions. Supported late transactional ordering is InstallExecute, RemoveExistingProducts, InstallFinalize. Placement after Finalize has different rollback semantics and is not selected.

sources.title: Changing the System State Using a Custom Action
sources.paraphrasedFinding: Use deferred CAs for system state change, with preceding rollback CAs. An immediate action may set metadata/properties; do not disguise marker mutation or broker launch as an unrestricted immediate cleanup action.

sources.title: Obtaining Context Information for Deferred Execution Custom Actions
sources.paraphrasedFinding: Deferred actions do not retain full original session context; pass bounded canonical CustomActionData, ProductCode and UserSID as documented. Commit actions cannot read ProductCode normally; UserSID is not a substitute for checking the actual process token.

sources.title: Custom Action Type2
sources.paraphrasedFinding: A Binary-table EXE is extracted temporarily; it does not depend on an installed file surviving uninstall. Nonzero exit is failure. Command line is not a safe secret transport and EXE exit is distinct from any child broker it launched.

sources.title: Custom Action Return Processing Options
sources.paraphrasedFinding: Default synchronous mode checks return; Continue hides failure and Async permits late work. Retain default checked synchronous CAs. A separately explicit broker is supervised by owned process handle and fixed IPC, never inferred finished from CA logical ACK.

sources.title: Using a Sequence Table
sources.paraphrasedFinding: Full/reduced UI sequences are not universal: execute sequence must enforce gate for silent/basic modes as well. Advertise/admin image paths are distinct and must be rejected or explicitly nonmutating.

sources.title: CreateFileW
sources.paraphrasedFinding: Share conflicts reject subsequent incompatible opens; restrictions persist until exact handles close across process contexts. An open shared app handle can block exclusive maintenance, while exclusive maintenance blocks new app opens. Exclude share-delete to pin inode/path; file existence alone does not show ownership.

sources.title: Terminating a Process
sources.paraphrasedFinding: Termination sets exit code and signals original process object; resources/handles close, but child processes do not automatically terminate. Retain the actual original process HANDLE; PID reuse, sent STOP, pipe EOF or a completion JSON are not physical process-return proof.

prohibitedInferences: commit CA cannot fail into rollback
rollback CA ACK is global rollback completion
a property or PID/file presence proves exact MSI owner
no-extra-package chainer and direct cached repair behavior already documented or tested
networkScope: Only read-only official Microsoft Learn pages; no install, API mutation, Windows or CI operation.
